frequency_question: How often does a recipient nation successfully operationalize domestic production of advanced foreign missile systems within 2 years of receipt?
membership_rule: Includes sovereign states receiving complex foreign cruise or precision-guided missile tech during active conflict that attempted indigenous assembly or manufacturing lines. Excludes simple maintenance depots or purely foreign-operated supply chains.
window: 2 years from technology transfer agreement or initiation of effort

cases.name: Taiwan Hsiung Feng production (US tech transfer context)

coverage_note: 4 named historical analogues; limited exact matches due to the rarity of high-tech cruise missile proliferation to actively invaded states.
known_gaps: Extremely high-tech systems like Storm Shadow/SCALP require specialized supply chains that differ from simpler turbojet cruise missiles.
skeleton: 4 major historical precedents for establishing complex cruise missile production under duress or foreign licensing
multiplier: 3 hits out of 4 historical analogues yielding a baseline frequency
validity_reason: Based on long-term defense industrial trends and proliferation speeds which evolve slowly.
